checks.title: L1 over-temperature, break-glass (single sensor > 38 C)
checks.requirement: Any single rack sensor above the hard limit must latch a break-glass trip and command the fast fallback ramp.
checks.method: Prime ARMED on safe data; inject one sensor at 39.5 C; assert immediate trip.

checks.title: L1 over-temperature, voted (2-of-3 trio > 32 C)
checks.requirement: Two of three sensors in a rack trio above the soft limit must latch a graded trip (single-sensor noise must not).
checks.method: Prime ARMED; inject a trio with two sensors at ~33 C; assert graded trip.

checks.title: Sensor watchdog (comms loss > 10 s)
checks.requirement: Loss of sensor data beyond the watchdog horizon must trip (blind => assume unsafe).
checks.method: Stop the sensor feed while MPC stays fresh; measure seconds to trip.

checks.title: MPC watchdog (missed control cycle > 90 s)
checks.requirement: A stalled advisory MPC must trip to the safe fallback rather than hold a stale setpoint indefinitely.
checks.method: Stop MPC proposals while sensors stay fresh; measure seconds to trip.

checks.title: Command validation (out-of-bounds / rate violation)
checks.requirement: A physically implausible MPC proposal (bounds or slew-rate) must be rejected by the relay before it reaches the plant.
checks.method: Feed an in-bounds proposal that jumps 0.20 in one cycle (> 0.15 slew limit); assert trip.

checks.title: Latch durability across restart
checks.requirement: A latched trip must survive an OOM/cold restart and refuse to re-arm without an explicit operator reset.
checks.method: Trip + persist; instantiate a fresh relay; restore; assert it boots TRIPPED.

checks.title: L2 model-residual interlock (acute CRAC loss)
checks.requirement: A divergence between the frozen clean-coil reference and the plant (acute cooling loss) must trip on the residual norm.
checks.method: Closed loop plant+reference+relay; inject -75% CRAC capacity; measure onset-to-trip.
checks.detail: latency is fault-onset -> first TRIPPED command, control-cycle resolution

checks.title: Dead-man revert on lost controller
checks.requirement: If the relay goes silent beyond the dead-man horizon, the plant must autonomously revert to the safe always-on baseline without any command.
checks.method: Apply an accepted command; age it past the horizon; assert the plant reverts to baseline within one cycle.

checks.title: Zombie fencing across failover (no dual-write)
checks.requirement: After failover, a resurrected ex-leader must not be able to write to the actuator; the single-writer invariant must hold by fencing, not by agreement.
checks.method: Leader A writes; A dies; standby B takes over (epoch bump); zombie A re-publishes at its stale epoch; assert the actuator applied only A then B, never the zombie.
checks.detail: enforcement is at plant-sim (the actuator), mirroring the dead-man philosophy

checks.title: Restart re-acquisition (fresh sequence accepted)
checks.requirement: A relay restart with a fresh in-memory sequence counter must be accepted by the actuator (epoch bumps per leadership session) and not rejected as a stale replay.
checks.method: Leader publishes seq 1..3; restart (same id) re-acquires; publishes seq 1; assert the epoch bumped and the fresh command is applied.

checks.title: Coil-health early warning precedes safety trip
checks.requirement: Slow coil fouling must raise a maintenance ALARM (advisory, not a trip) while the relay is still ARMED with airflow headroom — ahead of any acute trip.
checks.method: Closed loop with MPC; inject slow fouling; assert ALARM precedes any L2 trip by the minimum lead.
checks.detail: accelerated fouling rate for test; real lead scales ~1/rate (days/weeks)

checks.title: Coil-health load-shift false-alarm immunity
checks.requirement: A change of operating point (load) must not be mistaken for coil degradation; baselines are per-load-bin.
checks.method: Commission one load bin; shift to a different bin with a higher structural residual; assert no alarm.

scope_note:
This ledger is automatically generated conformance EVIDENCE for the ThermalFlow control and safety logic. It is produced by deterministic, seeded, in-process simulation that imports and exercises the production safety modules directly (the files hashed under provenance.code_digest). It is offered as a CONTRIBUTION to a deployer's technical documentation and is structured to the headings of EU AI Act Annex IV (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) for convenience.

It is NOT, and must not be represented as: (a) a legal determination that ThermalFlow is an 'AI system' or a 'high-risk AI system' under the Act; (b) a statement that Annex IV or any other obligation applies; (c) a conformity assessment, audit, or certification. Whether the Act applies, and under which Annex III category (e.g. safety components in the management of critical infrastructure), is a determination for the deployer's compliance/legal function. The authors are not lawyers and this is not legal advice.

Latencies reported here are CONTROL-LOOP-CYCLE figures under a modelled plant. They do NOT include message-bus transport, container scheduling, or physical-actuator response. Wall-clock latency on real infrastructure MUST be measured separately via a live-stack smoke test before any safety claim is made. The simulation covers control/safety LOGIC; it does not cover the messaging or orchestration layer. No warranty is given.
